title: Optimization Terminal Discrimination Record
description: runs/iter-N/confirmation.json (design spec 3.3, 3.5) -- the record of ONE round of TERMINAL DISCRIMINATION. The paper's Figure 1 names this state `discriminate`; this branch calls it `confirm`, and the behaviour here is the paper's: a shortlist S subset of X_valid is measured FRESHLY and its members are compared against each other, so the final comparison does not rest on the fitted response at all. Written by orchestrator.optimize.stage_runner._finish_confirm. shortlist.json is written next to it as a POINTER to this file (see shortlist.schema.json) so the finalists and their measurements have exactly one source of truth. This is the assumption-light half of the two-bound obligation: residual_regret_terminal lives here at delta_terminal, residual_regret_model lives in recommendation.json at delta_screen, and no artifact carries a combined number.

stage.description: The terminal-discrimination state's name in this branch. Constant because no other state writes this artifact.

iteration.description: The iteration index this round ran at. The terminal state can SELF-LOOP, so successive rounds land in successive iterations.

round.description: Which terminal round this is. Round r > 1 keeps the previous winner plus every challenger whose bound still exceeded epsilon -- exactly those that could still change the epsilon-optimal decision. The registered round cap and the budget guard are what terminate the loop; the interpreter never decides it.

finalists.description: The REALIZED shortlist and its fresh measurements, one entry per finalist that was scheduled.

key.description: Stable per-round finalist handle (f0, f1, ...). `bounds` and `terminal_bound.challenger` reference finalists by this key rather than repeating their levels.

why.description: Which rung of the seeding ladder seated this finalist -- the model's answer, the best measured valid configuration, a model top candidate, a round-r carry-over, or known_valid_baseline. Recorded so a reader can tell what the shortlist was PUTTING ON TRIAL from what it was TRUSTING.

samples.description: This finalist's usable fresh replicate values. Empty when every replicate was excluded.

status.description: Why this finalist left the running, not merely that it did. MEASURED INVALIDITY TRUMPS PREDICTION: a single measured violation excludes the finalist outright rather than being averaged away over its surviving replicates, because a configuration that is admissible only sometimes is not admissible. `infeasible` means a replicate was measured inadmissible (or rejected) -- real information about the design space, and the configuration should be struck off. `unmeasured` means the instrument could not measure an ADMISSIBLE configuration (timeout, crash, unparseable output) -- a re-run with a larger budget may recover it, and striking it off would be wrong. The two were one value (`excluded`) until a timed-out finalist was reported as though it had violated a constraint.

best.description: The winning finalist's `key`, or null when no finalist produced a valid measurement at all (which is a real outcome, not an error -- the report ladder then falls to `baseline` or `none`).

bounds.description: PER-CHALLENGER upper bounds against the winner alone, keyed by finalist key, each computed at delta_terminal with M=1. That is the right level for a `keep measuring this one?` screening decision and the WRONG level for a certificate -- the certified verdict reads terminal_bound.value (the simultaneous max) and never these. Round r+1 reads this to decide who is still in contention.

epsilon.description: The resolved epsilon-optimality tolerance residual_regret_terminal is compared against: the declared `pct` of the reference named by epsilon_reference (or the declared `abs`). Null only when there is no reference at all -- unknown, never 0.

epsilon_reference.description: WHICH reference a percentage epsilon was resolved against. `best_finalist`: the winning admissible finalist's fresh mean (the normal case). `best_observed`: no finalist was admissible, so the best measured ADMISSIBLE configuration so far (per-configuration feasibility; `levels`/`value` name it). `recommendation`: nothing admissible was measured, so the epsilon the fitting stage resolved in recommendation.json. `declared_abs`: an absolute epsilon needs no reference. `none`: nothing to take a percentage of, so epsilon is null (unknown) -- never 0, which can never certify and is not what the author declared.

residual_regret_terminal.description: R_delta(x) from terminal discrimination at delta_terminal (design spec 3.5) -- the simultaneous max over the ADMISSIBLE members of the realized shortlist, carrying nothing but their fresh measurements. Null when no finalist produced a valid measurement, when the bound was not estimable, or when ANY admissible finalist went unmeasured: that rival's U_t is unknown, so the max over the shortlist is unknown, and an unknown is not a zero (INV-SEM02) -- a survivors-only max would UNDERSTATE the regret against exactly the rival nobody measured. The survivors-only number is then recorded as terminal_bound_measured_only. UNAFFECTED by an INADMISSIBLE finalist: that one is outside X_valid, the bound over the admissible shortlist is still valid, and it is `certified` that the exclusion suppresses. Never collapsed with recommendation.json's residual_regret_model, which is a different number at a different delta from disjoint inputs.

terminal_bound.description: The full record behind residual_regret_terminal, including WHICH arithmetic ran. Recorded so a reader can tell which bound they are looking at rather than inferring it from the branch date: pairing that reached only the artifact would leave the campaign reporting the wider bound while claiming the narrower method.

challenger.description: The finalist KEY that attains the bound (a levels dict at the model stage). A key rather than a dict because this file already records every finalist's levels against its key, and two representations of one fact can drift apart.

method.description: bonferroni_one_sided_t_paired when common random numbers were actually shared (design spec 3.8), bonferroni_one_sided_welch_t otherwise. A campaign with no declared workload seed gets Welch deliberately: the paired form stays VALID when the seeds were not shared but loses efficiency, and worse, would record a paired method about an experiment that paired nothing.

certification_withheld.description: Why `certified` is false, as named reasons rather than an unexplained boolean -- so a reader can tell a bound that was simply too wide from a GLOBAL claim withheld because the delta_screen premise was broken, or from a shortlist that was never fully compared. Empty exactly when certified is true. `finalist_measured_infeasible` and `fit_exclusions_level_correlated` are the two premise-breaking reasons: both are evidence that the model's ranking is not tracking the constrained objective, so epsilon-optimality over X_valid is unearned even though residual_regret_terminal (a number over the admissible shortlist resting on fresh measurements and no model) remains valid and is still reported. `finalist_unmeasured` means an admissible finalist produced no usable measurement (timeout, crash, unparseable output): the comparison is incomplete, residual_regret_terminal is null, and the remedy is to re-run it rather than strike it off. `no_admissible_finalist` means EVERY finalist was measured inadmissible (each had at least one replicate violating a declared constraint): the measurements are valid and complete, there is simply no admissible configuration in this shortlist to bound, so it replaces `bound_not_computable` (which means too little data to estimate a bound) and is distinct from a NaN response (an instrumentation defect). `model_inadequate` means the latest fitting stage's lack-of-fit F on pure error rejected the registered response class (recommendation.json model_adequate: false): the shortlist was seeded from measured leaders and the ranking of a rejected surface, so nothing supports the delta_screen premise that screening did not exclude the winner (design spec 3.6 rung 3 sits below certification). The within-shortlist bound is still reported.

certified.description: The GLOBAL epsilon-optimality verdict over X_valid, which rests on Pr(wrong global decision) <= delta_screen + delta_terminal. False whenever ANY finalist was measured inadmissible, even if the within-shortlist bound came in at or below epsilon: an inadmissible finalist is direct evidence that the model's ranking is not tracking the CONSTRAINED objective, so the delta_screen premise (screening did not exclude the true optimum) does not hold and the sum bound is unearned. The within-shortlist number stays reported; only the global label is withheld.

paired.description: Whether replicate i of every finalist actually ran the same workload seed (common random numbers, design spec 3.8), set from the campaign's declared optimization.workload.seed_env. Forwarded to the bound computation, not merely recorded: the paired form works on DIFFERENCES so the workload's contribution cancels and the bound shrinks substantially.

delta_terminal.description: The terminal risk from the compiled policy's objective -- the delta this file's bound is stated at, kept distinct from delta_screen throughout.

excluded_infeasible.description: The levels of every finalist measured INADMISSIBLE (or rejected). Non-empty is what withholds `certified` above, so it is recorded rather than derived. The name predates the infeasible/unmeasured split and is kept for existing readers; it now contains only genuinely inadmissible finalists.

excluded_unmeasured.description: The levels of every finalist whose MEASUREMENT failed -- timeout, crash, unparseable output -- rather than being inadmissible. Also withholds `certified`, because the terminal comparison has no fresh samples for it either, but it carries the opposite authoring consequence from `excluded_infeasible`: re-run with a larger budget rather than strike the configuration off.

confirmed_at_levels.description: The WINNING finalist's levels. A legacy single-point field kept because readers of it exist (the harness's recommendation fallback, the guide's worked output, the report ladder's terminal rungs); it now names the winner rather than the only configuration run. Empty when there is no winner.

replicates.description: Total replicate runs scheduled this round, across all finalists.

usable_replicates.description: How many of those produced a usable measurement. The gap between this and `replicates` is what an exclusion looks like in aggregate.

mean.description: The winner's mean over its fresh replicates -- a MEASUREMENT, unlike recommendation.json's `predicted`. Null when there is no winner.

spread.description: Population standard deviation of the winner's replicates; 0.0 with fewer than two of them.

observations.description: The winner's individual replicate values, so the mean and spread above are auditable rather than asserted. Empty when there is no winner.

best_observed.description: OPTIONAL and present only when there is both a winner and a best measured valid configuration to compare it against. Two keys: `levels`, and the campaign's own PRIMARY METRIC NAME carrying that configuration's value -- so the second key is campaign-dependent and cannot be enumerated here, which is why this object stays open. `the best finalist` and `the best configuration found` are different claims, and recording both keeps the artifact honest when they disagree -- a mis-specified surface can leave the winner below a corner an earlier state measured.

confirmed_is_best_observed.description: OPTIONAL, written alongside best_observed: whether the winner actually matched or beat it.

regression_vs_best_observed.description: OPTIONAL, written ONLY when confirmed_is_best_observed is false -- the size of the shortfall. Its presence is the signal that the observed corner, not the winner, is the campaign's real answer and the surface is mis-specified -- UNLESS within_epsilon is true: a single earlier row is an upward-biased estimate of its configuration, and a gap inside the campaign's own indifference width is recorded rather than raised. Never written when the best observed row belongs to the winning configuration itself.

terminal_bound_measured_only.description: PRESENT ONLY when a finalist went unmeasured while the measured finalists still yielded a bound: that bound, over the measured finalists alone. Recorded because the comparison among the survivors genuinely happened; NOT residual_regret_terminal, because it is silent about the unmeasured rival(s) and would understate the regret.
